text:
Priya Nair: Following the PM, we need a lean customer comms flow and a hard link between public notes and postmortem actions. Who owns what and by when?

Ben Ortiz: I can own the statuspage snippets. My rough SLA proposal: 1) immediate banner (automated) within 5m, 2) short interim within 1h, 3) 24h update with scope, 4) 72h provisional summary with action items, 5) 30d closure note listing completed remediations.

Lina Park: Agree on the cadence. For the 72h provisional, require a filled "publish checklist" (owner, JIRA id, redaction level, outreach required?). We should also require the postmortem ticket to have at least one remediation owner for every Sev>2 action before publish.

Oscar Reed: Note on redaction policy from security: redact customer IDs and sample requests by default. We can include anonymized examples (aggregate stats) without legal review. Anything that could identify a customer or reveal data flow needs Level-2 review.

Priya Nair: Proposed redaction tiers (compact):
- Tier A: Metrics & non-identifying technical summary (auto)
- Tier B: Operational root cause & mitigations (eng sign-off)
- Tier C: Sensitive info / customer identifiers (legal + security)
- Tier D: Regulatory/external disclosures (exec + legal)

Ben Ortiz: Add explicit owners per tier: A = oncall, B = eng lead, C = legal+sec, D = product+exec. Also add maximum sign-off SLAs: eng 4h, legal 24h, exec 48h.

Lina Park: On recurring pattern detection: if a postmortem action label matches a recurring category (we'll use tags like "cache-thrashing", "kv-cache-evict", etc.) and the same tag appears in 3 incidents within 60 days, auto-flag "recurring" and create an engineering review epic. Owner of original action becomes initial triage owner unless they opt out.

Oscar Reed: For customer-facing language, let's standardize phrases to avoid accidental blame: prefer "we experienced" to "you may have seen"; avoid internal Jargon (no "OOM" without explanation). Provide a one-line customer TL;DR at top.

Priya Nair: Example 1-line TL;DR (draft): "We experienced elevated request errors between 14:0314:57 UTC that affected a subset of customers; mitigation applied and we'll follow up with a full summary within 72 hours."

Ben Ortiz: Will build templates for 5m banner, 1h interim, 24h, 72h, 30d. Templates will include required metadata fields: `postmortem_id`, `redaction_tier`, `owner`, `jira_link`, `customer_note_published` (y/n).

Lina Park: Action tracking integration: require the `customer_note_url` field in the JIRA ticket before clearing the last remediation task. Add a webhook that posts to #incidents when customer_note_published flips to true.

Oscar Reed: Security/legal SLA: legal to respond within 24 business hours for Tier C; if delayed, we publish a Tier-B summary redacted and mark Tier-C pending with expected ETA.

IncidentBot: Auto-rule applied: new postmortems must include `postmortem_id` and `severity` tags. Recurring detector threshold set to 3 incidents in 60 days.

Priya Nair: Can we also add a simple checklist for comms reviewers: 1) TL;DR present, 2) redaction tier checked, 3) owners listed and JIRA linked, 4) outreach required? Make that a required gating form on publish.

Ben Ortiz: Yep - I'll add the gating form to the draft flow and wire the webhook to require an ack from the owner before publish.

Lina Park: I'll update the postmortem playbook with the gating form and recurring incident handling rules. Target: playbook update + templates live by EOD.

Oscar Reed: I'll produce a short guidance doc for legal on what needs Tier-C review vs Tier-B redaction.

Priya Nair: Great. Owners please ack in thread so we can mark tasks.

Ben Ortiz: Ack. (building templates now)

Lina Park: Ack. (updating playbook)

Oscar Reed: Ack. (legal/sec guidance)

Priya Nair: Thanks team. I'll consolidate templates and create the JIRA epic INF-4899 to track rollout.

IncidentBot: Created epic INF-4899 and linked 3 postmortems for review.
